problem:
Find the Cartesian equation of the parabola defined by the parametric equations

$$
x=\frac{1}{6}t,\,y=\frac{1}{12}{t}^{2},\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

feedback.problem:
Consider the following parabola:

$$
x=\frac{1}{3}t,\,y=\frac{2}{9}{t}^{2},\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

The Cartesian equation of the parabola is

${x}^{2}=$
{{field-1}}.
feedback.worked_solution:
First, let's make $t$ the subject of the parametric equations. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}t & =3x,\,{t}^{2}=\frac{9y}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Squaring both sides of the first equation, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{2} & =9{x}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now eliminate the parameter $t$ by substituting the above into the equation ${t}^{2}=\frac{9y}{2}$ and rearranging to find the Cartesian equation of the parabola, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}9{x}^{2} & =\frac{9y}{2} \\ {x}^{2} & =\frac{1}{2}y\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the Cartesian equation of the parabola is ${x}^{2}=\frac{1}{2}y.$
